items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Spatial data input comes first; analysis comes after data are entered, verified and linked.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about overlay and buffer analysis in GIS is correct?
items.answer: Buffer analysis can be used to find areas within a specified distance of a road, river or facility.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: That is network analysis; buffer analysis creates zones at a given distance. Overlay combines two or more layers. Buffers can be created around points, lines and areas.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on GIS: components and spatial data formats and answer the questions that follow.
"Spatial data in a GIS are referenced to locations on the earth. Raster data have a simple data structure and overlay operations are easy to perform. The components of a GIS are hardware, software, data, people and procedures."
(i) Information about the population of a village stored in a table linked to its location is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'attribute data' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Raster data are convenient for overlay analysis. (1)
items.answer: (i) attribute data (ii) Non-spatial data that describe the characteristics of spatial features. (iii) Every layer has the same grid of cells, so cells can be combined directly.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) attribute data (ii) Non-spatial data that describe the characteristics of spatial features. (iii) Every layer has the same grid of cells, so cells can be combined directly.

items.stem:
Statement: Buffer analysis is used in planning services.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It shows which areas lie within a given distance of facilities such as schools, hospitals or roads.
items.markingKey: (d) It shows which areas lie within a given distance of facilities such as schools, hospitals or roads.
options: It integrates many types of data and allows queries and analysis of spatial relationships.
It combines several conditions such as land use, slope and soil to find areas that meet all of them.
Points, lines and polygons are defined precisely by coordinates.
It shows which areas lie within a given distance of facilities such as schools, hospitals or roads.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Raster data always need less storage than vector data.
Reason (R): Raster data have a simple data structure and overlay operations are easy to perform.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Raster data usually need large storage volumes. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by 'Geographic Information System' in the context of GIS: components and spatial data formats?
items.answer: A system for capturing, storing, checking, integrating, manipulating, analysing and displaying data that are spatially referenced to the earth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Geographic Information System correctly explained as a system for capturing, storing, checking, integrating, manipulating, analysing and displaying data that are spatially referenced to the earth.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about advantages of GIS and sequence of GIS activities:
I. Spatial analysis is the first step of GIS activities.
II. A GIS allows different scenarios to be tested for planning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Spatial data input comes first; analysis comes after data are entered, verified and linked. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about advantages of GIS and sequence of GIS activities:

items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Data can be updated easily. II is correct. III is correct.

III only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on overlay and buffer analysis in GIS and answer the questions that follow.
"Network analysis helps in finding the shortest or quickest routes. Overlay analysis can be used to identify suitable sites, for example for a new industry or school. Overlay analysis combines two or more layers to answer questions about places where conditions coincide."
(i) Finding the shortest route between two places on a road map in a GIS uses: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'network analysis' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Overlay analysis is useful for site selection. (1)
items.answer: (i) network analysis (ii) The GIS operation that analyses routes and connectivity along a network such as roads. (iii) It combines several conditions such as land use, slope and soil to find areas that meet all of them.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) network analysis (ii) The GIS operation that analyses routes and connectivity along a network such as roads. (iii) It combines several conditions such as land use, slope and soil to find areas that meet all of them.

Read the following extract on advantages of GIS and sequence of GIS activities and answer the questions that follow.
"The sequence of GIS activities includes spatial data input, entering attribute data, data verification and editing, linking spatial and attribute data, and spatial analysis. A GIS allows users to ask queries about locations and attributes. Data in a GIS can be updated easily."

items.answer: (i) Spatial data input (ii) The GIS activity of examining locations, attributes and relationships of features to answer queries. (iii) Errors in captured data would lead to wrong analysis and decisions.
